name: neurico-host-local-llm-fallback
description: "On the shared /data neurico host, API keys may be absent; GPUs are shared/contended; vLLM recipe, cached models, and pitfalls (pkill self-kill, cudnn clash, prompt_logprobs OOM)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: e7324b18-29e9-4db0-ae5a-a9f0cd196a49
  modified: 2026-10-16T18:23:14.513Z
---

Observed 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-16 in neurico research workspaces on this host:
- OPENROUTER_KEY / OPENAI keys were NOT set in the session env (`~/.flamebird/neurico/.env` has it commented out). Resource-finder stage may be skipped (no papers/, datasets/, code/).
- Local models + datasets cached in `/data/transformers/hub` (HF_HOME=/data/transformers): Qwen2.5-{0.5,1.5,3,7,14}B-Instruct safetensors, Qwen3/3.5 family, Llama-3.1-8B, GGUFs; datasets incl. glue(sst2 only), stanfordnlp/sst2, samsum, ag_news, boolq, mmlu. huggingface.co is reachable for extra downloads (curl resolve/main URLs).
- 2026-10-16: 4x RTX A6000 (48GB) present but shared — other users' jobs held ~42GB on 3 GPUs and intermittently grabbed the 4th. Approach that worked: vLLM 0.31 (`uv add "vllm>=0.10"`; unpinned `uv add vllm` resolved an ancient 0.4 build), small `gpu_memory_utilization` (~0.11 ≈ 5GB) for ≤1.5B models on the leftover slices, plus a bash wrapper that polls `nvidia-smi` free memory and retries launch. vLLM checks free mem ≥ util×total at startup.
- 2026-10-14 (no GPU then): llama.cpp multi-server CPU fallback worked; `transformers` CPU generation much slower.
- Pitfalls: `pkill -f <pattern>` inside a Bash call whose text contains the pattern kills the calling shell (find PIDs, kill by PID separately). Leftover `nvidia-cudnn-cu12` 8.x from a failed install breaks flashinfer ("Found 2 libcudnn.so.x") — `uv pip uninstall nvidia-cudnn-cu12`. vLLM `prompt_logprobs` materialises full-vocab logits → OOM on small slices; cap `max_num_batched_tokens` (~1024). Don't edit a bash script while a running loop is executing it.
- Label-restricted log-probs in vLLM: `logprobs_mode="processed_logprobs"` + `allowed_token_ids=label_ids` returns log-softmax renormalised over the labels.

Update 2026-10-16 (inter-model-agreement workspace): 4×A6000 present but shared — other neurico sessions keep each GPU at ~6–10 GB free, fluctuating second to second. What worked:
- `uv venv --python 3.12` (default 3.14 breaks vLLM); pyproject needs `requires-python="==3.12.*"` and `[tool.uv] package=false`.
- vLLM 0.31: no bitsandbytes; set `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` (JIT build fails); `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.
- Use pre-quantized 4-bit AWQ/GPTQ checkpoints (~5.5 GB for 8B): Qwen/*-AWQ, hugging-quants Llama-3.1/gemma-2 AWQ-INT4, tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Instruct-AWQ, solidrust Mistral AWQ, kaitchup Olmo-3/Phi-3 GPTQ.
- Cap gpu_memory_utilization to ~12.5 GB and retry on startup OOM via a scheduler loop; max_model_len 2560, max_num_seqs 64.
- Gated models in /data/transformers/hub (meta-llama Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, google/gemma-7b-it) have weights but no config/tokenizer → unusable; unsloth mirror of Llama-3.1 is complete. Disk /data is ~100% full.

Update 2026-10-16 (few-shot-ordering workspace, 2nd session): a "Begin research execution" prompt can land on a workspace where a prior session already finished most work (REPORT.md exists, background jobs killed at session end). Check logs/*.status and REPORT first and resume only the interrupted pieces rather than restarting. Monitor `tail -n0 -F` on status files missed an append; poll status files directly instead. Qwen2.5-14B bf16 (~30 GB) won't fit when GPUs have ≤23 GB free.

Update 2026-10-16 (system_prompt_residual_effects workspace): the neurico runner can kill a session at its 6h limit (return_code 143) and relaunch with the same prompt while detached background jobs (e.g. `run_all.sh`) keep running. On start, check for existing planning.md/REPORT.md, `*_PLACEHOLDER` markers, `.neurico/pipeline_*.json`, `*.partial` checkpoints and live PIDs before redoing anything; usually you only need to wait for the jobs and re-run the scoring/analysis.

- LoRA (r=64, bs=2, len 320) of a 1.5B model trains in a 5 GB slice (~5–8 min/epoch for ~2.9k docs).
- `pgrep -f "<pattern>"` inside a wait loop matches the loop's own bash command line → use `pgrep -f "[x]pattern"` bracket trick.
- Qwen2.5-3B as a yes/no paraphrase-equivalence judge rejected ~90% of good paraphrases; embedding cosine (all-mpnet-base-v2, cached) worked better.
- A retry loop's waiting must not count as failed tries (wrote gpu_run_wait.sh) — otherwise jobs give up while waiting for memory.

Update 2026-10-19 (decoding_strategy_sensitivity workspace, 11 models × 132k gens, vLLM 0.32):
- Killing a generate.py parent leaves its `VLLM::EngineCore` child orphaned (ppid 1) holding GPU memory — kill the EngineCore PID too.
- Size budgets by KV/token, not weights: Phi-3-mini (no GQA) at 6 GB had a 2.2k-token KV cache → ~1 seq concurrency, useless. Olmo-3-7B is also KV-heavy.
- A small idle slice (5–6 GB on a GPU at 0% util) beat a big slice on a GPU at 100% util shared with 4 jobs (Phi-3 GSM8K 12 min vs 40–80 min for 7B models on the busy GPU). Check `utilization.gpu`, not just free memory.
- In generate scripts, size gpu_memory_utilization from `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` minus ~1.2 GB (the parent's CUDA context counts), and bail if it's below ~75% of budget.
- `trust_remote_code=True` + HF_HUB_OFFLINE fails for checkpoints whose config auto_map points to a Hub repo (kaitchup Phi-3 GPTQ); use False (native arch).
- Qwen3-8B-AWQ (enable_thinking=False) works as a ~9 GB LLM judge: 17.6k rubric judgments in ~45 min, 0 parse failures.

Update 2026-10-20 (tokenizer_fertility_bias workspace, encoder fine-tuning on ~5 GB slices):
- No resource-finder output again; HF datasets with loading scripts (daily_dialog, banking77) fail — use parquet mirrors (`/api/datasets/<id>/parquet`) or the original CSV URLs in the script.
- 110M–180M encoders fine-tune fine in 3–5 GB (bs32, len128, bf16 autocast, ~1 min/run). ByT5-small needs ~10 GB even on short sentences and >1 h per 256-word doc run under contention, and collapsed to majority class with Adafactor lr 1e-3 / 3 epochs — budget it as infeasible on shared slices. CANINE also collapsed on short docs in 4/7 runs.
- Self-kill gotcha, bracket variant: `pgrep -f "[r]un_queue.py ../logs/jobs_long"` still killed the calling shell because the same Bash command later contained the literal text `run_queue.py ../logs/jobs_long.txt`. Find PIDs in one call, kill in a separate call.
- statsmodels formula GLM with a bool outcome column models P(False) (patsy treats it as categorical) → flipped signs; cast to int.
- Byte-level BPE (GPT-2/Llama/Qwen) offset_mapping includes the leading space; map tokens to words by the end offset.

Update 2026-10-20 (icl_label_bias workspace): GLUE in the cache has only sst2 — RTE/MRPC parquet downloads directly from `huggingface.co/datasets/nyu-mll/glue/resolve/main/<task>/<split>-00000-of-00001.parquet`. One GPU was fully free at session start and got taken within ~5 min, so launch the biggest model immediately. On a busy shared GPU, 7–8B AWQ at ~8.6 GB budget (eager) ran ~10k 600-token prompts in ~75 min; 14B bf16 took 74 min. Two wait-loops seeing the same free GPU simultaneously race and OOM — stagger launches (~2 min). Bootstrap ECE CIs via pd.concat per resample were >10 min; per-item bin sufficient statistics × multinomial weights was seconds.

Update 2026-10-20 (quantization_failure_modes workspace, 7 models × 7 RTN levels, vLLM 0.32):
- In-place weight edits inside vLLM work: `llm.collective_rpc(fn)` with `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1`, fn(self) touches `self.model_runner.model`; keep a CPU backup in the worker and quantize row-chunks (full-matrix fp32 temps OOM on slices). Disable prefix caching.
- Don't call `torch.cuda.mem_get_info()` in the vLLM parent — its CUDA context eats ~0.8 GB on GPU0 and startup then fails the free-memory check; get total via nvidia-smi.
- GPUs 0/1 top out at exactly 5125 MiB free (other users' 43 GB jobs) → budget ≤4.4 GB per slice. Multi-GPU TP rarely gets simultaneous slices; a queue with alternative configs ("1:9.5,2:4.4") was what worked. TP shards must keep quant groups aligned (Qwen2.5-3B intermediate 11008/4 not divisible by 128).
- HF `device_map` sharding needs `accelerate` installed (not pulled in by vllm).
- Self-kill again: `pkill -f`/`grep '[x]pat'` still matches if the SAME command line also contains the pattern elsewhere (e.g. a later nohup). Kill by PID in a separate call.
- Contended-GPU timings: 7–8B bf16 on a 20 GB slice ~2–8 min/level for 1.6k prompts once GPU2 freed (~17:00–19:00); Phi-3 (KV-heavy) on 13 GB of a 100%-util GPU took 33 min.

Update 2026-10-21 (cot_verbosity_threshold workspace): GPUs saturated all session (≤6 GB free, 7–8B AWQ at 8 GB never started in 40+ tries). The user's own long-lived `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --port 8011` (cascade venv, GPU3) was idle and usable via `/v1/completions` (raw prompt + stop strings; `stop_reason` returned) — check `curl 127.0.0.1:8011/v1/models` and `/metrics` num_requests_running before using; it gave the only 7B+ model and an LLM judge. For multi-round generation against a server, run each item's rounds in its own thread (synchronous batch rounds stall on stragglers: 4 min/round → 13 min total). New vLLM startup failure on contended GPUs: "Error in memory profiling … other processes release GPU memory" — just retry. HotpotQA distractor prompts reach ~2.4k tokens; use max_model_len ≥4096.

Update 2026-10-21 (context_window_decay workspace, long-context 1K–16K prompts):
- GPUs saturated again from ~13:00 (other neurico sessions + liuxiao TP job); GPU0/1 "5125 MiB free" is another job's fluctuating activation memory — launches there fail even when the check passes. A single scheduler (one launch per GPU per 120 s) beats per-job wait loops, which raced each other (4 OOMs at once when GPU2 briefly freed 29 GB).
- Startup-race fix that worked: in run_model.py, allocate a placeholder `torch.empty(budget+0.5 GB)` immediately, release it when the vLLM EngineCore child maps `libcuda.so` (poll /proc/<child>/maps every 50 ms). Guard with an env flag (HOLD_PARENT) — vLLM spawns EngineCore by re-importing __main__, so the hold code otherwise runs again in the child. Scheduler threshold: budget + 1.3 GB.
- 16K-token prompts: Qwen2.5-7B-AWQ on a busy shared GPU ≈3k tok/s → 2,880 prompts (18M tokens) took 1h40; budget runs by total prompt tokens. 0.5–1.5B on an idle slice: 5–15 min.
- `AMead10/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-AWQ` downloads in <1 min and runs in a ~4 GB slice up to ~9K context. Qwen3-0.6B (non-thinking) answers "number or name" questions with a number 95% of the time.

Update 2026-10-21 (cot_verbosity_tax workspace, 6+ concurrent neurico sessions): GPUs were ~fully oversubscribed; launches failed ~80% from free-memory races. Lessons:
- Long multi-round generation (budget forcing, 12 rounds × up to 2k tokens) on a 100%-util shared GPU is very slow: 7B-AWQ forced arm took ~4 h incl. a ~60 min final answer pass (small KV → ~15 concurrent long contexts). Budget for it, or cut rounds/items for ≥7B.
- My own jobs on the same GPU slow each other badly — don't stack 7B+14B+alt runs on one GPU.
- Two of my queues polling independently launched on the same GPU in the same second and both failed: use ONE queue. A queue restart loses track of its running children → mark them (EXTERNAL file) or it relaunches duplicates. Stop leftover launch.sh wrappers at session end (they relaunch after you kill the child).
- Qwen3-4B-AWQ (download ~2.5 GB) works as a 4.4 GB-slice LLM judge: ~1k rubric labels in ~4 min, 0 parse failures, but applies categories loosely — audit samples.
- pandas 3: groupby().apply drops grouping columns — restore them by index join.
- Background Bash with run_in_background still caps at 10 min when a timeout isn't given — set timeout explicitly for long waits.

Update 2026-10-21 (positional_retrieval_decay workspace): GPUs saturated again by ~6 parallel neurico sessions, each running retry loops that race for the same freed slices. What worked:
- **Retry engine creation in-process** (poll nvidia-smi, size budget = min(max, free−0.35), retry LLM() after failures) instead of relaunching; build prompts AFTER engine init to shrink the race window.
- **Work-stealing pool** (src/worker_pool.py): one thread per GPU launches the highest-priority job whose min budget fits; per-tag flock files prevent duplicates; exit code 75 = "gave up waiting" (not a failure). Chunked generation with append-only .partial files (whole samples) made kills/resumes safe and let analysis use partial runs.
- Duplicate-run gotcha: a "move finished .jsonl back to .partial" extension script raced a queue that retried the same tag → two writers on one file. Use the lock in every code path.
- 7–8B AWQ on a GPU shared by ~7 processes: 12–21 min per 720 prompts of avg 3K tokens; ≤3B models: 0.5–3 min. Budget large models at N/3.
- WikiText-103 test+val gives only ~49 passages of ≥7.5K words (~10K tokens) → a "16K" haystack silently capped at ~10K; check ctx_tokens per length.
- Single-needle retrieval is at ceiling for Qwen2.5 ≥1.5B / Llama-8B / Qwen3-4B up to 10K; near-miss distractors (same name, different type) are the discriminating condition.

Update 2026-10-21 (prompt_surface_sensitivity workspace, 10 models × 24k prompts, vLLM 0.32):
- Shared-GPU startup races were lost ~90% of the time (other sessions fill a freed slice during vLLM's ~20 s startup). What fixed it: TP=1 → `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0` (in-process engine) + grab memory with a `torch.empty(budget)` tensor as soon as free, and monkeypatch `vllm.v1.worker.gpu_worker.MemorySnapshot` to free the tensor + `empty_cache()` just before vLLM measures. TP=2 → per-GPU holder subprocesses + `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=fork` so forked workers inherit the patch and SIGKILL their GPU's holder. TP workers create CUDA ctx+NCCL (~0.8 GB) *before* the snapshot, so a 5.0 GB slice can't host TP; need ≥5.6 GB/GPU. Holders must exit when their parent dies (poll getppid), else orphans hog memory. Code: that workspace's src/generate.py, src/gpu_queue.py.
- Llama-3.x and Gemma-2 chat templates `| trim` message content (trailing whitespace is a no-op); Qwen2.5 keeps it — useful as a free placebo.
- vLLM greedy decoding is not batch-invariant: byte-identical prompts in different batch positions gave identical long (≤1024-tok) outputs only 23–76% of the time, moving IFEval accuracy by up to ~3 pp; short (≤10-tok) outputs ~99.7% identical.
- Two GPU queues launching TP jobs onto the same GPU pair race each other — run one queue.

Update 2026-10-22 (sampling_temp_misinformation workspace, 7 models × 9 temps × n=10, vLLM 0.32):
- GPU2 was fully free at 11:20 and ~37 GB of it was taken within 5 min — launch immediately.
- In-process hold (VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 + torch.empty placeholder + MemorySnapshot subclass patched in both
  `vllm.utils.mem_utils` and `vllm.v1.worker.gpu_worker`) started 3B/7B-AWQ jobs on the first try. Re-acquire the hold
  before each retry, or retries run without it and fail. Pick the GPU (max free) before importing torch, then pin to it.
- Qwen2.5-3B bf16 at an 8.5 GB budget (non-eager, 4096 batched tokens) → "No available memory for the cache blocks".
  3B-AWQ in 4.4 GB works.
- SamplingParams(n=10, seed=s) seeds the samples consecutively → requests with seeds s and s+1 share 9/10 streams
  (common random numbers across conditions). Space per-request seeds ≥ n apart if independence is wanted.
- GSM8K 512-token CoT × 81 samples × 400 items on a 100%-util shared GPU: 1.5–3 h per ≤3B model; the QA part takes minutes.
- Paired Wilcoxon on fractional, zero-heavy item-level diffs (sample-mean minus 0/1) contradicts the bootstrap CIs;
  use a sign-flip permutation test of the mean.

Update 2026-10-22 (embedding_drift_finetuning workspace, LoRA fine-tuning 160M–7B on shared GPUs):
- A fully free GPU (48 GB) at session start was reservable with a tiny holder (`torch.empty(36GB)` + exit on a RELEASE file) while code was written; have the training script touch RELEASE after loading weights to CPU, just before `.cuda()`. But whatever you don't hold gets taken within minutes, and the 7B LoRA run (17 GB) still OOM'd mid-run when co-tenants grew — budget 7B training as infeasible unless a GPU is dedicated. On a GPU at 100% util shared with another user, 7B LoRA bs4×512 ran ~7 s/step; 3B 4.6 s/step; 1.5B 2.9 s/step; checkpoint evals (1.6k probes + 1,070 MCQ items) 4–8.5 min. 0.5B LoRA fits a 5 GB slice (2.4 GB peak, 20 min/3k steps); 1.5B peaks 4.5 GB.
- "Idle" 5–6 GB slices at 0% util are transient: other users' 41–43 GB jobs regrow and OOM you minutes later.
- Worker queue bug: a worker that retries the first unclaimed job starves smaller jobs if that job never fits → per-job memory need + skip; and when killing a worker loop, its job lock dir is orphaned (rmdir it). Writing reps before accuracy evals means a mid-eval kill leaves a checkpoint with reps but no metrics — filter to steps present in metrics.jsonl.
- Science gotcha: always log held-out in-domain loss — Pythia-160M LoRA (r64, α128, lr 2e-4) diverged in every domain, and Qwen2.5 base on codeparrot Python showed no in-domain gain; "drift" results otherwise get misread.

Update 2026-10-23 (repetition_penalty_sideeffects workspace): GPU2 showed 48 GB free at 12:21 but was taken before vLLM was even installed (~10 min) — the uv install of vllm took >10 min (run it in background immediately). 7B-AWQ at 6.3–8.4 GB never started all session (all GPUs ≤1.5 GB free from 12:40); ≤3B AWQ at 4.2 GB ran fine. The user's `vllm serve Qwen3-8B` on :8011 had only ~2% KV usage at 24 concurrent requests — use 48–64 concurrency (~6 gen/s for 300-token outputs; LLM-judge ~75–100 calls/min). It accepts `repetition_penalty` and `chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: false}` in /v1/chat/completions. HF `model.generate` with a custom LogitsProcessor (1–1.5B bf16, bs 50, 320 new tokens) took 5–45 s/batch on a shared slice — fine for ablations vLLM can't express.

Update 2026-10-23 (batch_size_inference_quality workspace, 10 configs × 1,700 prompts × 7 batch conditions, vLLM 0.32):
- GPU2 showed 48 GB free at 12:22 but a sibling session (3 neurico sessions start together at 12:00) took 40 GB within ~1 min — the free GPU at session start is a race you'll usually lose; plan for ~5 GB slices.
- Killing a job to restart it with different settings loses its slice within seconds (other sessions' wait-loops grab it) — prefer env/file-driven behaviour changes decided at launch; unpinned (no CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES) relaunch with a smaller budget got a slice again.
- Static-chunk batching in one engine (`llm.generate(chunk_of_B)`) is a clean batch-size manipulation. B=1 eager on a shared GPU: ~50–60 min (0.5–1.5B) for 1,700 prompts incl. 700 × ≤512-token CoT; 3B bf16 B=4 ~2 h → budget B=1 on subsets for ≥3B.
- Result worth reusing: vLLM bf16 greedy is deterministic for an identical schedule (0 diffs) but batch-dependent: B=1 vs B≥4 changes 47–76% of CoT outputs; fp16 ~5× and fp32 ~12× fewer; divergences start at bf16 top-2 ties (logprob margin 0 or 0.125).
- Analysis gotcha: iterating `set(a) & set(b)` of string ids gives PYTHONHASHSEED-dependent order → bootstrap CIs not reproducible; sort first.

Update 2026-10-23 (system_prompt_saturation workspace, 9 models × 3.6k prompts up to 8k tokens, vLLM 0.32):
- GPU2 fully free at 12:20; grabbed it with a chunked holder (1 GB tensors, target size read from a control file) — but
  the 9 GB freed between two of my jobs was taken by other sessions within ~1 min, and later jobs got only 5–13 GB.
- vLLM memory profiling charges other tenants' growth during startup to *your* "non-torch" usage (8B AWQ at 13 GB got
  1.1 GB KV → startup ValueError). Fix: `LLM(kv_cache_memory_bytes=...)` skips profiling entirely; size the hold as
  weights + KV + ~1.5 GB.
- Holder handoff bugs: compute the holder's *actual* size from `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps` for its PID, not the
  target file; and on a 100%-full GPU, CUDA context creation raises `torch.AcceleratorError` (a RuntimeError), not
  OutOfMemoryError — catch both and wait for the holder to free before touching CUDA.
- Per-output-file `fcntl.flock` in generate.py (print "LOCKED … 0 to do" and exit 0) made several queues on different
  GPUs safe against duplicate writers.
- Timings on a GPU shared by ~8 processes: 8B AWQ with a 3.5 GB KV (28k tokens) needed 3 h for 3.6k prompts (1.2k of
  them 1–8k tokens); 14B AWQ with 13.6k-token KV couldn't finish long prompts at all. Short-prompt experiments for
  big models first, long-context ones only if KV ≥ ~20k tokens.
- Greedy re-run of Qwen2.5-1.5B on a different GPU/KV size: 13% byte-identical texts but rule-check agreement 93.7%
  and mean metric within 0.07 pp.

# Planning: LoRA Rank Selection Blind Spots

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
LoRA is the default way to adapt LLMs, and nearly every recipe hard-codes a rank (r=8 or 16) without justification.
If the best rank really varies by an order of magnitude across tasks, practitioners are systematically leaving
accuracy on the table for "hard" generative tasks (math, code) or wasting parameters/memory on easy ones. A cheap,
pre-training predictor of the needed rank (e.g. from gradients at initialization) would remove a costly sweep.

### Gap in Existing Work
(No literature review was pre-gathered for this workspace; the following is from background knowledge.)
- Hu et al. 2021 (LoRA) reported that very low ranks (r=1–8) suffice on GPT-3 for NLU/NLG benchmarks and that ΔW has
  very low "intrinsic rank"; Aghajanyan et al. 2020 showed low intrinsic dimensionality of fine-tuning, decreasing with
  model size.
- Later work (AdaLoRA, Zhang et al. 2023; rsLoRA, Kalajdzievski 2023; "LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less",
  Biderman et al. 2024) found that code / math continued-training needs much higher rank, and that the standard
  alpha/r scaling makes high ranks under-perform unless learning rate / scaling is adjusted.
- What is missing: a *controlled* sweep that (a) holds data budget, optimizer and evaluation fixed across several task
  types and model sizes, (b) quantifies the cost of the r=8 default per task with uncertainty, and (c) tests whether a
  cheap, label-free-of-training statistic (spectrum of the full-weight gradient at init) predicts the knee rank.

### Our Novel Contribution
A controlled rank sweep (r = 1…128, 8 values) on 6 tasks spanning classification → math → code, on two model sizes of
one family (Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B base), plus a gradient-spectrum predictor evaluated by Spearman correlation against the
empirically determined knee rank.

### Experiment Justification
- Exp 1 (rank sweep, 0.5B, 6 tasks × 8 ranks × 2 seeds): needed to measure per-task optimal/knee rank and the rank-8 gap (H1, H2).
- Exp 2 (rank sweep, 1.5B, same grid): needed to test whether the knee shifts with model size (H3) and to add
  data points for the predictor test.
- Exp 3 (gradient intrinsic dimensionality at init per task × model): the proposed predictor (H4).
- Exp 4 (learning-rate sensitivity at selected ranks): a rank comparison at a single lr is confounded by the fact that
  the optimal lr depends on rank under alpha=2r scaling; we check whether conclusions survive per-rank lr tuning.

## Research Question
Does the optimal LoRA rank vary widely across tasks, how much does the common default (r=8) cost, does the knee rank
shrink with model size, and can the effective rank of the initial full-weight gradient predict it?

## Hypothesis Decomposition
- H1: max/min knee rank across tasks (per model) ≥ 8.
- H2: for the "high-rank" tasks, metric(best rank) − metric(r=8) is 3–8 pp (bootstrap CI excludes 0).
- H3: knee(1.5B) < knee(0.5B) on the same task for most tasks (paired, sign test).
- H4: Spearman(grad-ID, knee rank) > 0.7 over (task, model) pairs; a single calibrated scale puts the prediction
  within a factor 2 of the knee for most pairs.

## Proposed Methodology

### Approach
Base models: Qwen2.5-0.5B and Qwen2.5-1.5B (base, same family/tokenizer → clean size comparison; both fit the ~4–6 GB
GPU slices available on this shared host). 3B only if a GPU frees up.

Tasks (all converted to causal-LM SFT with loss only on the response tokens; 4,000 training examples each, 1 epoch):
| task | train | eval | metric |
|---|---|---|---|
| SST-2 sentiment | GLUE train | validation (872) | accuracy (label-restricted scoring) |
| Emotion (6-way) | dair-ai/emotion train | test (1,000 sample) | accuracy |
| AG News (4-way) | train | test (1,000 sample) | accuracy |
| BoolQ | train | validation (1,000 sample) | accuracy |
| GSM8K | train | test (all 1,319) | exact-match of final answer (greedy) |
| Python code | python_code_instructions_18k | MBPP test (500) | pass@1 by executing the 3 tests |
Every run also reports held-out target-token NLL (300 held-out training-distribution examples), a lower-noise
secondary metric.

LoRA config: all linear layers (q,k,v,o,gate,up,down), alpha = 2r (constant scale 2, the "r=8, alpha=16" convention),
dropout 0.05, AdamW lr 2e-4, cosine with 3% warmup, effective batch 16, max length 512, bf16 autocast.
Ranks: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128. Seeds: 2 (0.5B), ≥1 (1.5B; second seed if time). Zero-shot (r=0) baseline.

### Definitions (pre-registered)
- Best rank: argmax of seed-averaged metric.
- Knee rank: smallest r whose seed-mean metric ≥ best − δ, δ = max(0.5 pp, 1 pooled SE of the metric between seeds/
  sampling). Also reported with δ = 1 pp, and on NLL (smallest r within 1% of the best relative NLL reduction gain).
- Rank-8 gap: best − r8, paired bootstrap over eval items (and seeds).
- Gradient ID: for every target matrix, accumulate the full-weight gradient of the SFT loss at the pretrained weights
  over 128 training examples; compute the singular-value spectrum; r90 = #singular values capturing 90% of the
  squared Frobenius norm. Predictor = median r90 over matrices (secondary: entropy effective rank, r50, r99,
  stable rank, top-8 energy fraction).

### Baselines
Zero-shot base model; the r=8 default; best-rank oracle. Predictor baselines: constant prediction (r=8) and the
zero-shot error rate of the task as a naive "difficulty" predictor.

### Statistical Analysis Plan
Paired bootstrap (10k resamples over eval items, seeds pooled) for gaps; Spearman with permutation p-value for H4;
sign test for H3; α = 0.05, Holm correction across the 6 tasks for the gap tests.

## Expected Outcomes
Supportive: classification knees at r≤4, GSM8K/code knees ≥32, rank-8 gap 3–8 pp on GSM8K/code, smaller knees for
1.5B, ρ > 0.7. Refuting: flat curves (all knees ≤8), or gaps within noise, or ρ ≤ 0.

## Timeline and Milestones
Setup + code 1 h; 0.5B sweep ~2 h on 3–4 slices in parallel; 1.5B sweep ~2–3 h; grad-ID 20 min; analysis + report 1 h.

## Potential Challenges
- Shared GPUs (~4–6 GB free): use a work queue that launches jobs only when free memory fits; gradient checkpointing
  for 1.5B; per-output flock to avoid duplicate writers.
- Noise between neighbouring ranks larger than effects → knee tolerance, 2 seeds, NLL secondary metric.
- Fixed-lr confound → Exp 4.

## Success Criteria
All four sub-hypotheses receive a clear supported / not supported verdict with CIs, documented in REPORT.md.

"""Train one LoRA adapter (model, task, rank, seed, lr) and evaluate it.

Writes results/runs/<tag>.json with config, training curve, held-out NLL and per-item eval correctness.
rank 0 = zero-shot base model (no training).
"""
import argparse
import fcntl
import json
import math
import os
import random
import sys
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from tasks import load_task, extract_gsm_answer, gsm_correct, extract_code  # noqa: E402
from code_exec import run_tests  # noqa: E402

WS = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
MODELS = {"0.5B": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B", "1.5B": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B", "3B": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B"}
TARGETS = ["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj", "gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj"]
MAX_LEN = 512


def set_seed(s):
    random.seed(s)
    np.random.seed(s)
    torch.manual_seed(s)
    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(s)


def encode(tok, ex):
    """Tokenize prompt+target+eos; labels only on target/eos tokens. Truncate from the left of the prompt if needed."""
    p = tok(ex["prompt"], add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
    t = tok(ex["target"], add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"] + [tok.eos_token_id]
    t = t[:MAX_LEN - 16]
    p = p[-(MAX_LEN - len(t)):]
    return p + t, [-100] * len(p) + t


def collate(batch, pad_id):
    L = max(len(x[0]) for x in batch)
    ids = torch.full((len(batch), L), pad_id, dtype=torch.long)
    lab = torch.full((len(batch), L), -100, dtype=torch.long)
    att = torch.zeros((len(batch), L), dtype=torch.long)
    for i, (a, b) in enumerate(batch):
        ids[i, :len(a)] = torch.tensor(a)
        lab[i, :len(b)] = torch.tensor(b)
        att[i, :len(a)] = 1
    return ids, lab, att


def lm_loss(model, ids, lab, att, reduction="mean"):
    """Causal-LM loss computed only at labelled positions (avoids materialising full-vocab logits for prompts)."""
    inner = model.get_base_model() if hasattr(model, "get_base_model") else model
    h = inner.model(input_ids=ids, attention_mask=att).last_hidden_state
    h = h[:, :-1]
    y = lab[:, 1:]
    m = y != -100
    logits = inner.lm_head(h[m]).float()
    loss = F.cross_entropy(logits, y[m], reduction="sum")
    if reduction == "mean":
        return loss / m.sum()
    return loss, m.sum()


@torch.no_grad()
def heldout_nll(model, data, pad_id, bs=8):
    model.eval()
    tot, n = 0.0, 0
    for i in range(0, len(data), bs):
        ids, lab, att = [x.cuda() for x in collate(data[i:i + bs], pad_id)]
        with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
            l, c = lm_loss(model, ids, lab, att, reduction="sum")
        tot += l.item()
        n += c.item()
    return tot / n


@torch.no_grad()
def eval_cls(model, tok, items, labels, bs=16):
    model.eval()
    lab_ids = [tok(" " + l, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"][0] for l in labels]
    assert len(set(lab_ids)) == len(lab_ids), "label first tokens collide"
    tok.padding_side = "left"
    correct = []
    for i in range(0, len(items), bs):
        chunk = items[i:i + bs]
        enc = tok([c["prompt"] for c in chunk], return_tensors="pt", padding=True, truncation=True,
                  max_length=MAX_LEN).to("cuda")
        inner = model.get_base_model() if hasattr(model, "get_base_model") else model
        with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
            h = inner.model(**enc).last_hidden_state[:, -1]
            logits = inner.lm_head(h).float()[:, lab_ids]
        pred = logits.argmax(-1).tolist()
        correct += [int(p == c["label"]) for p, c in zip(pred, chunk)]
    return correct, None


@torch.no_grad()
def generate(model, tok, prompts, max_new, stop, bs):
    model.eval()
    tok.padding_side = "left"
    outs = [None] * len(prompts)
    order = sorted(range(len(prompts)), key=lambda i: -len(prompts[i]))  # length-sorted batches
    for s in range(0, len(order), bs):
        idx = order[s:s + bs]
        enc = tok([prompts[i] for i in idx], return_tensors="pt", padding=True).to("cuda")
        with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
            g = model.generate(**enc, max_new_tokens=max_new, do_sample=False, pad_token_id=tok.pad_token_id,
                               eos_token_id=tok.eos_token_id, stop_strings=stop, tokenizer=tok)
        texts = tok.batch_decode(g[:, enc["input_ids"].shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True)
        for i, t in zip(idx, texts):
            outs[i] = t
    return outs


def evaluate(model, tok, T, gen_bs):
    if T["kind"] == "cls":
        return eval_cls(model, tok, T["eval"], T["labels"])
    if T["kind"] == "gsm8k":
        outs = generate(model, tok, [e["prompt"] for e in T["eval"]], 320, ["\nQuestion:"], gen_bs)
        corr = [int(gsm_correct(extract_gsm_answer(o), e["answer"])) for o, e in zip(outs, T["eval"])]
        return corr, outs
    if T["kind"] == "code":
        outs = generate(model, tok, [e["prompt"] for e in T["eval"]], 384, ["\n###"], gen_bs)
        codes = [extract_code(o) for o in outs]
        corr = [int(x) for x in run_tests(codes, T["eval"])]
        return corr, outs
    raise ValueError(T["kind"])


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="0.5B")
    ap.add_argument("--task", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--rank", type=int, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-4)
    ap.add_argument("--alpha_mult", type=float, default=2.0, help="alpha = alpha_mult * r (standard scaling)")
    ap.add_argument("--rslora", action="store_true", help="use alpha/sqrt(r) scaling instead of alpha/r")
    ap.add_argument("--epochs", type=float, default=1.0)
    ap.add_argument("--bs", type=int, default=16, help="effective batch size")
    ap.add_argument("--micro_bs", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--grad_ckpt", type=int, default=-1)
    ap.add_argument("--out_dir", default=os.path.join(WS, "results", "runs"))
    ap.add_argument("--tag", default="")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    tag = a.tag or f"{a.model}_{a.task}_r{a.rank}_s{a.seed}_lr{a.lr:g}" + ("_rs" if a.rslora else "")
    os.makedirs(a.out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    out_path = os.path.join(a.out_dir, tag + ".json")
    if os.path.exists(out_path):
        print("EXISTS", out_path)
        return
    lock = open(out_path + ".lock", "w")
    try:
        fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
    except OSError:
        print("LOCKED", out_path)
        return

    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
    from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model

    t0 = time.time()
    set_seed(a.seed)
    T = load_task(a.task)
    path = MODELS[a.model]
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(path)
    if tok.pad_token is None:
        tok.pad_token = tok.eos_token
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(path, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).cuda()
    long_task = a.task in ("gsm8k", "code", "boolq")
    grad_ckpt = a.grad_ckpt if a.grad_ckpt >= 0 else int(a.model != "0.5B")
    micro = a.micro_bs or (4 if long_task else 8)
    gen_bs = 64 if a.model == "0.5B" else 32

    curve = []
    if a.rank > 0:
        cfg = LoraConfig(r=a.rank, lora_alpha=a.alpha_mult * a.rank, lora_dropout=0.05, target_modules=TARGETS,
                         use_rslora=a.rslora, task_type="CAUSAL_LM")
        model = get_peft_model(model, cfg)
        if grad_ckpt:
            model.gradient_checkpointing_enable(gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={"use_reentrant": False})
            model.enable_input_require_grads()
        params = [p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad]
        n_trainable = sum(p.numel() for p in params)
        opt = torch.optim.AdamW(params, lr=a.lr, weight_decay=0.0, betas=(0.9, 0.999))
        data = [encode(tok, ex) for ex in T["train"]]
        accum = a.bs // micro
        steps = int(math.ceil(len(data) * a.epochs / a.bs))
        warm = max(1, int(0.03 * steps))
        sched = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LambdaLR(
            opt, lambda s: (s + 1) / warm if s < warm else 0.5 * (1 + math.cos(math.pi * (s - warm) / max(1, steps - warm))))
        rng = random.Random(a.seed)
        order = []
        while len(order) < steps * a.bs:
            perm = list(range(len(data)))
            rng.shuffle(perm)
            order += perm
        model.train()
        run_loss = 0.0
        for step in range(steps):
            for k in range(accum):
                bidx = order[step * a.bs + k * micro: step * a.bs + (k + 1) * micro]
                ids, lab, att = [x.cuda() for x in collate([data[i] for i in bidx], tok.pad_token_id)]
                with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
                    loss = lm_loss(model, ids, lab, att) / accum
                loss.backward()
                run_loss += loss.item()
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(params, 1.0)
            opt.step()
            sched.step()
            opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            if (step + 1) % 10 == 0 or step == steps - 1:
                curve.append((step + 1, run_loss / 10))
                if (step + 1) % 50 == 0:
                    print(f"step {step+1}/{steps} loss {run_loss/10:.4f} {time.time()-t0:.0f}s", flush=True)
                run_loss = 0.0
        if grad_ckpt:
            model.gradient_checkpointing_disable()
    else:
        n_trainable, steps = 0, 0
    t_train = time.time() - t0
    nll = heldout_nll(model, [encode(tok, ex) for ex in T["heldout"]], tok.pad_token_id)
    corr, outs = evaluate(model, tok, T, gen_bs)
    res = {
        "tag": tag, "model": a.model, "task": a.task, "rank": a.rank, "seed": a.seed, "lr": a.lr,
        "alpha_mult": a.alpha_mult, "rslora": a.rslora, "epochs": a.epochs, "bs": a.bs, "steps": steps,
        "n_trainable": n_trainable, "heldout_nll": nll, "metric": float(np.mean(corr)), "n_eval": len(corr),
        "correct": corr, "curve": curve, "train_time_s": t_train, "total_time_s": time.time() - t0,
        "peak_mem_gb": torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() / 1e9,
    }
    with open(out_path + ".tmp", "w") as f:
        json.dump(res, f)
    os.replace(out_path + ".tmp", out_path)
    if outs is not None:
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(WS, "results", "outputs"), exist_ok=True)
        with open(os.path.join(WS, "results", "outputs", tag + ".json"), "w") as f:
            json.dump(outs, f)
    print(f"DONE {tag} metric={res['metric']:.4f} nll={nll:.4f} train={t_train:.0f}s total={res['total_time_s']:.0f}s "
          f"peak={res['peak_mem_gb']:.2f}GB", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

rank 0 = zero-shot base model (no training).

import fcntl
import json
import math

import random
import sys

MAX_LEN = 512


def set_seed(s):
    random.seed(s)
    np.random.seed(s)

def encode(tok, ex):
    """Tokenize prompt+target+eos; labels only on target/eos tokens. Truncate from the left of the prompt if needed."""
    p = tok(ex["prompt"], add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
    t = tok(ex["target"], add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"] + [tok.eos_token_id]
    t = t[:MAX_LEN - 16]
    p = p[-(MAX_LEN - len(t)):]
    return p + t, [-100] * len(p) + t


def collate(batch, pad_id):
    L = max(len(x[0]) for x in batch)
    ids = torch.full((len(batch), L), pad_id, dtype=torch.long)
    lab = torch.full((len(batch), L), -100, dtype=torch.long)
    att = torch.zeros((len(batch), L), dtype=torch.long)
    for i, (a, b) in enumerate(batch):
        ids[i, :len(a)] = torch.tensor(a)
        lab[i, :len(b)] = torch.tensor(b)
        att[i, :len(a)] = 1
    return ids, lab, att


def lm_loss(model, ids, lab, att, reduction="mean"):
    """Causal-LM loss computed only at labelled positions (avoids materialising full-vocab logits for prompts)."""
    inner = model.get_base_model() if hasattr(model, "get_base_model") else model
    h = inner.model(input_ids=ids, attention_mask=att).last_hidden_state
    h = h[:, :-1]
    y = lab[:, 1:]
    m = y != -100
    logits = inner.lm_head(h[m]).float()
    loss = F.cross_entropy(logits, y[m], reduction="sum")

def heldout_nll(model, data, pad_id, bs=8):
    model.eval()

"""Gradient intrinsic dimensionality at initialization.

For each LoRA target matrix W (all 7 linear types in every layer) accumulate the full-weight gradient of the SFT
loss at the pretrained weights over N examples (same prompt/target format as training), then compute its singular
value spectrum. Summaries per matrix: r50/r90/r99 (#singular values capturing that fraction of squared Frobenius
energy), entropy effective rank (Roy & Vetterli 2007), stable rank ||G||_F^2/||G||_2^2, and the energy fraction
captured by the top-8 directions (what a rank-8 first step could represent).

To fit small GPU slices, gradients are computed for one group of layers at a time (repeated forward/backward passes).
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import random
import sys

import numpy as np
import torch

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from tasks import load_task  # noqa: E402
from train_eval import MODELS, TARGETS, encode, collate, lm_loss, set_seed  # noqa: E402

WS = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


def spectrum_stats(G):
    s = torch.linalg.svdvals(G.float().cuda()).double()
    e = s ** 2
    tot = e.sum()
    c = torch.cumsum(e, 0) / tot
    p = s / s.sum()
    ent = -(p[p > 0] * torch.log(p[p > 0])).sum()
    out = {f"r{int(q*100)}": int((c < q).sum().item()) + 1 for q in (0.5, 0.9, 0.99)}
    out["erank"] = float(torch.exp(ent))
    out["stable_rank"] = float(tot / e[0])
    out["top8_energy"] = float(c[min(7, len(c) - 1)])
    out["dim"] = min(G.shape)
    return out, s[:256].float().cpu().numpy().tolist()


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="0.5B")
    ap.add_argument("--task", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=128)
    ap.add_argument("--micro_bs", type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument("--layer_groups", type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    out_path = os.path.join(WS, "results", "grad_id", f"{a.model}_{a.task}_n{a.n}_s{a.seed}.json")
    if os.path.exists(out_path):
        print("EXISTS", out_path)
        return
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path), exist_ok=True)
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
    set_seed(a.seed)
    T = load_task(a.task)
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODELS[a.model])
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODELS[a.model], torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).cuda()
    model.gradient_checkpointing_enable(gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={"use_reentrant": False})
    model.enable_input_require_grads()
    for p in model.parameters():
        p.requires_grad_(False)
    ex = random.Random(a.seed).sample(T["train"], a.n)
    data = [encode(tok, e) for e in ex]
    layers = model.model.layers
    nL = len(layers)
    groups = np.array_split(np.arange(nL), a.layer_groups)
    per_matrix = []
    spectra = {}
    for g in groups:
        mats = {}
        for li in g:
            for name in TARGETS:
                mod = getattr(layers[li].self_attn, name, None) or getattr(layers[li].mlp, name)
                mod.weight.requires_grad_(True)
                mats[(int(li), name)] = mod.weight
        acc = {k: torch.zeros_like(w, dtype=torch.float32) for k, w in mats.items()}
        model.train()  # dropout is 0 in Qwen2.5; train mode only matters for checkpointing
        ntok = 0
        for i in range(0, len(data), a.micro_bs):
            ids, lab, att = [x.cuda() for x in collate(data[i:i + a.micro_bs], tok.pad_token_id)]
            with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
                loss, c = lm_loss(model, ids, lab, att, reduction="sum")
            loss.backward()
            ntok += c.item()
            for k, w in mats.items():
                acc[k] += w.grad.float()
                w.grad = None
        for k, w in mats.items():
            w.requires_grad_(False)
            G = acc[k] / ntok  # gradient of the mean token loss
            st, sv = spectrum_stats(G)
            st.update({"layer": k[0], "module": k[1], "fro": float(G.norm())})
            per_matrix.append(st)
            spectra[f"{k[0]}.{k[1]}"] = sv
        del acc
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        print(f"group {g.tolist()} done", flush=True)
    keys = ["r50", "r90", "r99", "erank", "stable_rank", "top8_energy"]
    summary = {k: float(np.median([m[k] for m in per_matrix])) for k in keys}
    # Frobenius-weighted mean (matrices with larger gradients dominate the first update)
    w = np.array([m["fro"] for m in per_matrix]) ** 2
    summary.update({f"{k}_fw": float(np.sum(w * np.array([m[k] for m in per_matrix])) / w.sum()) for k in keys})
    res = {"model": a.model, "task": a.task, "n": a.n, "seed": a.seed, "summary": summary,
           "per_matrix": per_matrix, "spectra": spectra}
    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(res, f)
    print("DONE", a.model, a.task, json.dumps(summary))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

loss at the pretrained weights over N examples (same prompt/target format as training), then compute its singular
value spectrum. Summaries per matrix: r50/r90/r99 (#singular values capturing that fraction of squared Frobenius
energy), entropy effective rank (Roy & Vetterli 2007), stable rank ||G||_F^2/||G||_2^2, and the energy fraction
captured by the top-8 directions (what a rank-8 first step could represent).

To fit small GPU slices, gradients are computed for one group of layers at a time (repeated forward/backward passes).
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import random
import sys

import numpy as np
import torch

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from tasks import load_task  # noqa: E402
from train_eval import MODELS, TARGETS, encode, collate, lm_loss, set_seed  # noqa: E402

WS = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


def spectrum_stats(G):
    s = torch.linalg.svdvals(G.float().cuda()).double()
    e = s ** 2
    tot = e.sum()
    c = torch.cumsum(e, 0) / tot
    p = s / s.sum()
    ent = -(p[p > 0] * torch.log(p[p > 0])).sum()
    out = {f"r{int(q*100)}": int((c < q).sum().item()) + 1 for q in (0.5, 0.9, 0.99)}
    out["erank"] = float(torch.exp(ent))
    out["stable_rank"] = float(tot / e[0])
    out["top8_energy"] = float(c[min(7, len(c) - 1)])
    out["dim"] = min(G.shape)
    return out, s[:256].float().cpu().numpy().tolist()


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="0.5B")
    ap.add_argument("--task", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=128)
    ap.add_argument("--micro_bs", type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument("--layer_groups", type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    out_path = os.path.join(WS, "results", "grad_id", f"{a.model}_{a.task}_n{a.n}_s{a.seed}.json")
    if os.path.exists(out_path):
        print("EXISTS", out_path)
        return
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path), exist_ok=True)
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
    set_seed(a.seed)
    T = load_task(a.task)
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODELS[a.model])
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODELS[a.model], torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).cuda()
    model.gradient_checkpointing_enable(gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={"use_reentrant": False})
    model.enable_input_require_grads()
    for p in model.parameters():
        p.requires_grad_(False)
    ex = random.Random(a.seed).sample(T["train"], a.n)
    data = [encode(tok, e) for e in ex]
    layers = model.model.layers
    nL = len(layers)
    groups = np.array_split(np.arange(nL), a.layer_groups)
    per_matrix = []
    spectra = {}
    for g in groups:
        mats = {}
        for li in g:
            for name in TARGETS:
                mod = getattr(layers[li].self_attn, name, None) or getattr(layers[li].mlp, name)
                mod.weight.requires_grad_(True)
                mats[(int(li), name)] = mod.weight
        acc = {k: torch.zeros_like(w, dtype=torch.float32) for k, w in mats.items()}
        model.train()  # dropout is 0 in Qwen2.5; train mode only matters for checkpointing
        ntok = 0
        for i in range(0, len(data), a.micro_bs):
            ids, lab, att = [x.cuda() for x in collate(data[i:i + a.micro_bs], tok.pad_token_id)]
            with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
                loss, c = lm_loss(model, ids, lab, att, reduction="sum")
            loss.backward()
            ntok += c.item()
            for k, w in mats.items():
                acc[k] += w.grad.float()
                w.grad = None
        for k, w in mats.items():
            w.requires_grad_(False)
            G = acc[k] / ntok  # gradient of the mean token loss
            st, sv = spectrum_stats(G)
            st.update({"layer": k[0], "module": k[1], "fro": float(G.norm())})
            per_matrix.append(st)
            spectra[f"{k[0]}.{k[1]}"] = sv
        del acc
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        print(f"group {g.tolist()} done", flush=True)
    keys = ["r50", "r90", "r99", "erank", "stable_rank", "top8_energy"]
    summary = {k: float(np.median([m[k] for m in per_matrix])) for k in keys}
    # Frobenius-weighted mean (matrices with larger gradients dominate the first update)
    w = np.array([m["fro"] for m in per_matrix]) ** 2
    summary.update({f"{k}_fw": float(np.sum(w * np.array([m[k] for m in per_matrix])) / w.sum()) for k in keys})
    res = {"model": a.model, "task": a.task, "n": a.n, "seed": a.seed, "summary": summary,
           "per_matrix": per_matrix, "spectra": spectra}
    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(res, f)
    print("DONE", a.model, a.task, json.dumps(summary))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Single work queue over shared GPUs.

Jobs file: one job per line: `<mem_gb>\t<out_json_path>\t<command>`. The scheduler repeatedly picks the first job
(in file order = priority) whose output does not exist, that is not running, and whose memory need fits the free
memory on some GPU (per nvidia-smi, minus a margin), then launches it with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES set. At most one launch
per GPU every LAUNCH_GAP seconds (lets the new process allocate before the next decision). Failed jobs are retried up
to MAX_TRIES times. The jobs file is re-read every loop, so jobs can be appended while the queue runs.
"""
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

MARGIN_GB = 0.4
LAUNCH_GAP = 75
MAX_TRIES = 4


def free_mem():
    out = subprocess.run(["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=index,memory.free", "--format=csv,noheader,nounits"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    return {int(l.split(",")[0]): float(l.split(",")[1]) / 1024 for l in out.strip().splitlines()}


def read_jobs(path):
    jobs = []
    for line in open(path):
        line = line.rstrip("\n")
        if not line.strip() or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        mem, out, cmd = line.split("\t")
        jobs.append((float(mem), out, cmd))
    return jobs


def main(jobs_path, log_dir, gpus):
    os.makedirs(log_dir, exist_ok=True)
    running = {}  # out -> (proc, gpu, mem)
    tries = {}
    last_launch = {g: 0.0 for g in gpus}
    while True:
        for out, (p, g, m) in list(running.items()):
            if p.poll() is not None:
                del running[out]
                if p.returncode != 0 or not os.path.exists(out):
                    tries[out] = tries.get(out, 0) + 1
                    print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] FAIL rc={p.returncode} try={tries[out]} {out}", flush=True)
                else:
                    print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] OK {out}", flush=True)
        jobs = read_jobs(jobs_path)
        pending = [j for j in jobs if not os.path.exists(j[1]) and j[1] not in running and tries.get(j[1], 0) < MAX_TRIES]
        if not pending and not running:
            print("ALL DONE", flush=True)
            return
        fm = free_mem()
        now = time.time()
        for g in gpus:
            if now - last_launch[g] < LAUNCH_GAP:
                continue
            avail = fm.get(g, 0) - MARGIN_GB
            for mem, out, cmd in pending:
                if mem <= avail:
                    name = os.path.basename(out).replace(".json", "")
                    lf = open(os.path.join(log_dir, name + ".log"), "a")
                    env = dict(os.environ, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=str(g), PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:True")
                    p = subprocess.Popen(cmd, shell=True, stdout=lf, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, env=env)
                    running[out] = (p, g, mem)
                    last_launch[g] = now
                    pending.remove((mem, out, cmd))
                    print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] LAUNCH gpu{g} free={fm.get(g):.1f}GB need={mem} {name}", flush=True)
                    break
        time.sleep(10)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], [int(x) for x in sys.argv[3].split(",")])

"""Analysis of the rank sweep: knee/best ranks, rank-8 gaps, model-size comparison, gradient-ID predictor.

Outputs: results/summary_table.csv, results/knees.csv, results/gaps.csv, results/predictor.json, figures/*.png
"""
import glob
import json
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402

WS = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
R = os.path.join(WS, "results")
FIG = os.path.join(WS, "figures")
os.makedirs(FIG, exist_ok=True)
RANKS = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128]
TASKS = ["sst2", "emotion", "ag_news", "boolq", "gsm8k", "code"]
MODELS = ["0.5B", "1.5B"]
MAIN_LR = 2e-4
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)


def load_runs():
    rows = []
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(R, "runs", "*.json"))):
        d = json.load(open(f))
        rows.append(d)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def item_matrix(df, model, task, rank, lr=MAIN_LR, rslora=False):
    """(n_seeds, n_items) correctness matrix for one cell."""
    sub = df[(df.model == model) & (df.task == task) & (df["rank"] == rank) & np.isclose(df.lr, lr) & (df.rslora == rslora)]
    sub = sub.sort_values("seed")
    if len(sub) == 0:
        return None, []
    return np.array(sub.correct.tolist(), dtype=float), sub.seed.tolist()


def knee_from_curve(means, ses, ranks, min_delta=0.005):
    """Smallest rank whose mean is within delta of the best; delta = max(min_delta, SE of best)."""
    best_i = int(np.nanargmax(means))
    delta = max(min_delta, ses[best_i])
    for r, m in zip(ranks, means):
        if m >= means[best_i] - delta:
            return r, ranks[best_i], delta
    return ranks[best_i], ranks[best_i], delta


def main():
    df = load_runs()
    df = df[~df.rslora]
    main_df = df[np.isclose(df.lr, MAIN_LR)]
    # ---------- summary table ----------
    summ = (main_df.groupby(["model", "task", "rank"])
            .agg(metric=("metric", "mean"), metric_sd=("metric", "std"), nll=("heldout_nll", "mean"),
                 n_seeds=("seed", "nunique"), n_trainable=("n_trainable", "first"), train_time=("train_time_s", "mean"))
            .reset_index())
    summ.to_csv(os.path.join(R, "summary_table.csv"), index=False)

    # ---------- knees ----------
    knees = []
    for model in MODELS:
        for task in TASKS:
            s = summ[(summ.model == model) & (summ.task == task) & (summ["rank"] > 0)].set_index("rank")
            if not set(RANKS) <= set(s.index):
                continue
            means, ses = [], []
            for r in RANKS:
                M, _ = item_matrix(main_df, model, task, r)
                pm = M.mean(0)  # per-item mean over seeds
                means.append(pm.mean())
                # SE combining item sampling and seed variance (bootstrap over items of the seed-mean)
                ses.append(pm.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(pm)))
            means = np.array(means)
            k05, best, delta = knee_from_curve(means, ses, RANKS, 0.005)
            k1, _, _ = knee_from_curve(means, [0] * len(RANKS), RANKS, 0.01)
            nll = s.loc[RANKS, "nll"].values
            z = summ[(summ.model == model) & (summ.task == task) & (summ["rank"] == 0)]
            nll0 = z.nll.values[0] if len(z) else np.nan
            gain = nll0 - nll
            k_nll95 = RANKS[int(np.argmax(gain >= 0.95 * gain.max()))]
            k_nll99 = RANKS[int(np.argmax(gain >= 0.99 * gain.max()))]
            knees.append(dict(model=model, task=task, best_rank=best, knee=k05, knee_delta=delta, knee_1pp=k1,
                              knee_nll95=k_nll95, knee_nll99=k_nll99, best_nll_rank=RANKS[int(np.argmin(nll))],
                              best_metric=means.max(), r8_metric=means[RANKS.index(8)],
                              zero_shot=z.metric.values[0] if len(z) else np.nan,
                              n_seeds=int(s.n_seeds.min())))
    knees = pd.DataFrame(knees)
    knees.to_csv(os.path.join(R, "knees.csv"), index=False)
    print(knees.to_string())

    # ---------- rank-8 gaps (paired bootstrap over items) ----------
    gaps = []
    for _, k in knees.iterrows():
        M8, seeds8 = item_matrix(main_df, k.model, k.task, 8)
        Mb, seedsb = item_matrix(main_df, k.model, k.task, k.best_rank)
        d = Mb.mean(0) - M8.mean(0)
        boots = np.array([d[rng.integers(0, len(d), len(d))].mean() for _ in range(5000)])
        row = dict(model=k.model, task=k.task, best_rank=k.best_rank, gap_naive=d.mean(),
                   ci_lo=np.percentile(boots, 2.5), ci_hi=np.percentile(boots, 97.5),
                   p_boot=2 * min((boots <= 0).mean(), (boots >= 0).mean()))
        # cross-fitted gap: pick best rank on one seed, measure on the other (removes winner's-curse bias)
        if len(seeds8) >= 2:
            cf = []
            for sel, ev in [(0, 1), (1, 0)]:
                m_sel = [item_matrix(main_df, k.model, k.task, r)[0][sel].mean() for r in RANKS]
                rb = RANKS[int(np.argmax(m_sel))]
                cf.append(item_matrix(main_df, k.model, k.task, rb)[0][ev].mean() - M8[ev].mean())
            row["gap_crossfit"] = float(np.mean(cf))
        # gap of the best *larger* rank (is there anything to gain above 8?)
        hi = [r for r in RANKS if r > 8]
        mh = [item_matrix(main_df, k.model, k.task, r)[0].mean() for r in hi]
        row["gap_best_above8"] = max(mh) - M8.mean()
        gaps.append(row)
    gaps = pd.DataFrame(gaps)
    p = gaps.p_boot.values
    order = np.argsort(p)
    holm = np.empty_like(p)
    running = 0
    for i, j in enumerate(order):
        running = max(running, min(1, (len(p) - i) * p[j]))
        holm[j] = running
    gaps["p_holm"] = holm
    gaps.to_csv(os.path.join(R, "gaps.csv"), index=False)
    print(gaps.to_string())

    # ---------- figures: metric and NLL vs rank ----------
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 6, figsize=(22, 7))
    colors = {"0.5B": "#1f77b4", "1.5B": "#d62728"}
    for j, task in enumerate(TASKS):
        for model in MODELS:
            s = summ[(summ.model == model) & (summ.task == task) & (summ["rank"] > 0)].sort_values("rank")
            if len(s) == 0:
                continue
            per_seed = main_df[(main_df.model == model) & (main_df.task == task) & (main_df["rank"] > 0)]
            axes[0, j].plot(s["rank"], 100 * s.metric, "o-", color=colors[model], label=model)
            axes[0, j].scatter(per_seed["rank"], 100 * per_seed.metric, color=colors[model], s=8, alpha=0.4)
            z = summ[(summ.model == model) & (summ.task == task) & (summ["rank"] == 0)]
            if len(z):
                axes[0, j].axhline(100 * z.metric.values[0], color=colors[model], ls=":", lw=1)
            axes[1, j].plot(s["rank"], s.nll, "o-", color=colors[model], label=model)
            kk = knees[(knees.model == model) & (knees.task == task)]
            if len(kk):
                axes[0, j].axvline(kk.knee.values[0], color=colors[model], ls="--", lw=1, alpha=0.6)
        for i in range(2):
            axes[i, j].set_xscale("log", base=2)
            axes[i, j].set_xticks(RANKS)
            axes[i, j].set_xticklabels(RANKS)
            axes[i, j].axvline(8, color="gray", lw=0.8, alpha=0.4)
        axes[0, j].set_title(task)
        axes[1, j].set_xlabel("LoRA rank r")
    axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("eval metric (%)\n(dotted = zero-shot, dashed = knee)")
    axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("held-out target NLL (nats/token)")
    axes[0, 0].legend()
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "rank_curves.png"), dpi=130)
    plt.close()

    # ---------- gradient ID predictor ----------
    gid = []
    for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(R, "grad_id", "*.json")):
        d = json.load(open(f))
        gid.append(dict(model=d["model"], task=d["task"], **d["summary"]))
    if gid:
        gid = pd.DataFrame(gid)
        m = knees.merge(gid, on=["model", "task"])
        pred = {}
        preds = ["r50", "r90", "r99", "erank", "stable_rank", "top8_energy", "r90_fw", "erank_fw", "zero_shot"]
        for target in ["knee", "best_rank", "knee_nll95", "knee_nll99"]:
            for pc in preds:
                x = m[pc].values.astype(float)
                if pc in ("top8_energy", "zero_shot"):
                    x = -x  # less top-8 energy / lower zero-shot accuracy -> expected higher rank
                y = np.log2(m[target].values.astype(float))
                if len(m) < 4 or np.std(y) == 0:
                    continue
                rho, _ = stats.spearmanr(x, y)
                perm = np.array([stats.spearmanr(x, rng.permutation(y))[0] for _ in range(5000)])
                p = (np.abs(perm) >= abs(rho)).mean()
                # factor-of-2 accuracy with a leave-one-out calibrated log-linear map log2(knee) = a + b*log2(x)
                within2 = None
                if pc not in ("top8_energy", "zero_shot"):
                    lx = np.log2(np.maximum(m[pc].values.astype(float), 1e-9))
                    hits = []
                    for i in range(len(m)):
                        msk = np.arange(len(m)) != i
                        a = np.mean(y[msk] - lx[msk])  # slope fixed at 1: pure scale calibration
                        hits.append(abs((a + lx[i]) - y[i]) <= 1)
                    within2 = float(np.mean(hits))
                pred[f"{target}~{pc}"] = dict(rho=float(rho), p_perm=float(p), n=len(m), within2_loo=within2)
        # baseline: always predict rank 8
        for target in ["knee", "best_rank", "knee_nll95"]:
            pred[f"{target}~const8"] = dict(within2=float(np.mean(np.abs(np.log2(m[target]) - 3) <= 1)))
        json.dump(pred, open(os.path.join(R, "predictor.json"), "w"), indent=1)
        m.to_csv(os.path.join(R, "knees_with_gradid.csv"), index=False)
        for k, v in pred.items():
            print(k, v)
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.5))
        for ax, (pc, target) in zip(axes, [("r90", "knee"), ("r90", "knee_nll95"), ("erank", "knee")]):
            for model, mk in [("0.5B", "o"), ("1.5B", "s")]:
                mm = m[m.model == model]
                ax.scatter(mm[pc], mm[target], marker=mk, label=model, s=50)
                for _, r in mm.iterrows():
                    ax.annotate(r.task, (r[pc], r[target]), fontsize=8, xytext=(3, 3), textcoords="offset points")
            ax.set_yscale("log", base=2)
            ax.set_xlabel(f"gradient {pc} at init (median over matrices)")
            ax.set_ylabel(target)
            key = f"{target}~{pc}"
            if key in pred:
                ax.set_title(f"Spearman rho={pred[key]['rho']:.2f} (p={pred[key]['p_perm']:.2f})")
            ax.legend()
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "gradid_vs_knee.png"), dpi=130)
        plt.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Analysis of the rank sweep: knee/best ranks, rank-8 gaps, model-size comparison, gradient-ID predictor.

Outputs: results/summary_table.csv, results/knees.csv, results/gaps.csv, results/predictor.json, figures/*.png
"""
import glob
import json
import os

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402

WS = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
R = os.path.join(WS, "results")
FIG = os.path.join(WS, "figures")
os.makedirs(FIG, exist_ok=True)
RANKS = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128]
TASKS = ["sst2", "emotion", "ag_news", "boolq", "gsm8k", "code"]
MODELS = ["0.5B", "1.5B"]
MAIN_LR = 2e-4
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)


def load_runs():
    rows = []
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(R, "runs", "*.json"))):
        d = json.load(open(f))
        rows.append(d)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def item_matrix(df, model, task, rank, lr=MAIN_LR, rslora=False):
    """(n_seeds, n_items) correctness matrix for one cell."""
    sub = df[(df.model == model) & (df.task == task) & (df["rank"] == rank) & np.isclose(df.lr, lr) & (df.rslora == rslora)]
    sub = sub.sort_values("seed")
    if len(sub) == 0:
        return None, []
    return np.array(sub.correct.tolist(), dtype=float), sub.seed.tolist()


def knee_from_curve(means, ses, ranks, min_delta=0.005):
    """Smallest rank whose mean is within delta of the best; delta = max(min_delta, SE of best)."""
    best_i = int(np.nanargmax(means))
    delta = max(min_delta, ses[best_i])
    for r, m in zip(ranks, means):
        if m >= means[best_i] - delta:
            return r, ranks[best_i], delta
    return ranks[best_i], ranks[best_i], delta


def main():
    df = load_runs()
    df = df[~df.rslora]
    main_df = df[np.isclose(df.lr, MAIN_LR)]
    # ---------- summary table ----------
    summ = (main_df.groupby(["model", "task", "rank"])
            .agg(metric=("metric", "mean"), metric_sd=("metric", "std"), nll=("heldout_nll", "mean"),
                 n_seeds=("seed", "nunique"), n_trainable=("n_trainable", "first"), train_time=("train_time_s", "mean"))
            .reset_index())
    summ.to_csv(os.path.join(R, "summary_table.csv"), index=False)

    # ---------- knees ----------
    knees = []
    for model in MODELS:
        for task in TASKS:
            s = summ[(summ.model == model) & (summ.task == task) & (summ["rank"] > 0)].set_index("rank")
            if not set(RANKS) <= set(s.index):
                continue
            means, ses = [], []
            for r in RANKS:
                M, _ = item_matrix(main_df, model, task, r)
                pm = M.mean(0)  # per-item mean over seeds
                means.append(pm.mean())
                # SE combining item sampling and seed variance (bootstrap over items of the seed-mean)
                ses.append(pm.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(pm)))
            means = np.array(means)
            k05, best, delta = knee_from_curve(means, ses, RANKS, 0.005)
            k1, _, _ = knee_from_curve(means, [0] * len(RANKS), RANKS, 0.01)
            nll = s.loc[RANKS, "nll"].values
            z = summ[(summ.model == model) & (summ.task == task) & (summ["rank"] == 0)]
            nll0 = z.nll.values[0] if len(z) else np.nan
            gain = nll0 - nll

            k_nll99 = RANKS[int(np.argmax(gain >= 0.99 * gain.max()))]
            knees.append(dict(model=model, task=task, best_rank=best, knee=k05, knee_delta=delta, knee_1pp=k1,
                              knee_nll95=k_nll95, knee_nll99=k_nll99, best_nll_rank=RANKS[int(np.argmin(nll))],
                              best_metric=means.max(), r8_metric=means[RANKS.index(8)],
                              zero_shot=z.metric.values[0] if len(z) else np.nan,
                              n_seeds=int(s.n_seeds.min())))
    knees = pd.DataFrame(knees)
    knees.to_csv(os.path.join(R, "knees.csv"), index=False)
    print(knees.to_string())

    # ---------- rank-8 gaps (paired bootstrap over items) ----------
    gaps = []
    for _, k in knees.iterrows():
        M8, seeds8 = item_matrix(main_df, k.model, k.task, 8)
        Mb, seedsb = item_matrix(main_df, k.model, k.task, k.best_rank)
        d = Mb.mean(0) - M8.mean(0)
        boots = np.array([d[rng.integers(0, len(d), len(d))].mean() for _ in range(5000)])
        row = dict(model=k.model, task=k.task, best_rank=k.best_rank, gap_naive=d.mean(),
                   ci_lo=np.percentile(boots, 2.5), ci_hi=np.percentile(boots, 97.5),
                   p_boot=2 * min((boots <= 0).mean(), (boots >= 0).mean()))
        # cross-fitted gap: pick best rank on one seed, measure on the other (removes winner's-curse bias)
        if len(seeds8) >= 2:
            cf = []
            for sel, ev in [(0, 1), (1, 0)]:
                m_sel = [item_matrix(main_df, k.model, k.task, r)[0][sel].mean() for r in RANKS]
                rb = RANKS[int(np.argmax(m_sel))]
                cf.append(item_matrix(main_df, k.model, k.task, rb)[0][ev].mean() - M8[ev].mean())
            row["gap_crossfit"] = float(np.mean(cf))
        # gap of the best *larger* rank (is there anything to gain above 8?)
        hi = [r for r in RANKS if r > 8]
        mh = [item_matrix(main_df, k.model, k.task, r)[0].mean() for r in hi]
        row["gap_best_above8"] = max(mh) - M8.mean()

        holm[j] = running

            axes[0, j].plot(s["rank"], 100 * s.metric, "o-", color=colors[model], label=model)
            axes[0, j].scatter(per_seed["rank"], 100 * per_seed.metric, color=colors[model], s=8, alpha=0.4)
            z = summ[(summ.model == model) & (summ.task == task) & (summ["rank"] == 0)]
            if len(z):
                axes[0, j].axhline(100 * z.metric.values[0], color=colors[model], ls=":", lw=1)
            axes[1, j].plot(s["rank"], s.nll, "o-", color=colors[model], label=model)
            kk = knees[(knees.model == model) & (knees.task == task)]
            if len(kk):
                axes[0, j].axvline(kk.knee.values[0], color=colors[model], ls="--", lw=1, alpha=0.6)
        for i in range(2):
            axes[i, j].set_xscale("log", base=2)
            axes[i, j].set_xticks(RANKS)
            axes[i, j].set_xticklabels(RANKS)
            axes[i, j].axvline(8, color="gray", lw=0.8, alpha=0.4)
        axes[0, j].set_title(task)
        axes[1, j].set_xlabel("LoRA rank r")
    axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("eval metric (%)\n(dotted = zero-shot, dashed = knee)")
    axes[1, 0].set_ylabel("held-out target NLL (nats/token)")
    axes[0, 0].legend()
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "rank_curves.png"), dpi=130)
    plt.close()

    # ---------- gradient ID predictor ----------
    gid = []
    for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(R, "grad_id", "*.json")):
        d = json.load(open(f))
        gid.append(dict(model=d["model"], task=d["task"], **d["summary"]))
    if gid:
        gid = pd.DataFrame(gid)
        m = knees.merge(gid, on=["model", "task"])
        pred = {}
        preds = ["r50", "r90", "r99", "erank", "stable_rank", "top8_energy", "r90_fw", "erank_fw", "zero_shot"]
        for target in ["knee", "best_rank", "knee_nll95", "knee_nll99"]:
            for pc in preds:
                x = m[pc].values.astype(float)
                if pc in ("top8_energy", "zero_shot"):
                    x = -x  # less top-8 energy / lower zero-shot accuracy -> expected higher rank
                y = np.log2(m[target].values.astype(float))
                if len(m) < 4 or np.std(y) == 0:

                p = (np.abs(perm) >= abs(rho)).mean()
                # factor-of-2 accuracy with a leave-one-out calibrated log-linear map log2(knee) = a + b*log2(x)
                within2 = None
                if pc not in ("top8_energy", "zero_shot"):
                    lx = np.log2(np.maximum(m[pc].values.astype(float), 1e-9))
                    hits = []

                        msk = np.arange(len(m)) != i
                        a = np.mean(y[msk] - lx[msk])  # slope fixed at 1: pure scale calibration
                        hits.append(abs((a + lx[i]) - y[i]) <= 1)
                    within2 = float(np.mean(hits))
                pred[f"{target}~{pc}"] = dict(rho=float(rho), p_perm=float(p), n=len(m), within2_loo=within2)
        # baseline: always predict rank 8
        for target in ["knee", "best_rank", "knee_nll95"]:
            pred[f"{target}~const8"] = dict(within2=float(np.mean(np.abs(np.log2(m[target]) - 3) <= 1)))
        json.dump(pred, open(os.path.join(R, "predictor.json"), "w"), indent=1)
        m.to_csv(os.path.join(R, "knees_with_gradid.csv"), index=False)
        for k, v in pred.items():
            print(k, v)
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4.5))

import re
p='results/jobs_main.txt'; L=open(p).read().splitlines()
def key(l):
    o=l.split('\t')[1]; b=o.split('/')[-1]
    gid='grad_id' in o
    m=re.match(r'(0\.5B|1\.5B)_(\w+?)_(?:r(\d+)_s(\d+)|n128)',b)
    model,task=m.group(1),m.group(2)
    tasks=["code","gsm8k","boolq","ag_news","emotion","sst2"]
    ti=tasks.index(task)
    rorder=[8,128,1,32,2,64,4,16]
    if gid: return ((0 if model=='0.5B' else 3), 2.5, 0, ti)
    r=int(m.group(3)); s=int(m.group(4))
    block={('0.5B',0):0,('0.5B',1):2,('1.5B',0):1}[(model,s)]
    if model=='1.5B': block=4
    if model=='0.5B' and s==1: block=5
    ri=rorder.index(r) if r>0 else 1.5
    return (block, ri, 0, ti)
L.sort(key=key)
open(p,'w').write('\n'.join(L)+'\n')
for l in L[:20]+L[54:64]: print(l.split('\t')[0], l.split('\t')[1].split('/')[-1])
EOF

long_task = a.task in ("gsm8k", "code", "boolq")
    grad_ckpt = a.grad_ckpt if a.grad_ckpt >= 0 else 1
    micro = a.micro_bs or (4 if long_task else 16)
    gen_bs = 64 if a.model == "0.5B" else 32

    curve = []
    if a.rank > 0:
        cfg = LoraConfig(r=a.rank, lora_alpha=a.alpha_mult * a.rank, lora_dropout=0.05, target_modules=TARGETS,
                         use_rslora=a.rslora, task_type="CAUSAL_LM")
        model = get_peft_model(model, cfg)
        adapter_dir = os.path.join(WS, "results", "adapters", tag)
        n_trainable = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(adapter_dir, "state.pt")):
            # resume after an eval-time failure: reuse the trained adapter
            ck = torch.load(os.path.join(adapter_dir, "state.pt"))
            missing = model.load_state_dict(ck["lora"], strict=False)
            assert not [k for k in missing.unexpected_keys], missing.unexpected_keys
            curve, steps, t_resume = ck["curve"], ck["steps"], ck["train_time"]
            print("loaded trained adapter from", adapter_dir, flush=True)
        else:
            t_resume = None
    if a.rank > 0 and t_resume is None:
        if grad_ckpt:
            model.gradient_checkpointing_enable(gradient_checkpointing_kwargs={"use_reentrant": False})
            model.enable_input_require_grads()
        params = [p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad]
        opt = torch.optim.AdamW(params, lr=a.lr, weight_decay=0.0, betas=(0.9, 0.999))
        data = [encode(tok, ex) for ex in T["train"]]
        accum = a.bs // micro
        steps = int(math.ceil(len(data) * a.epochs / a.bs))
        warm = max(1, int(0.03 * steps))
        sched = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LambdaLR(
            opt, lambda s: (s + 1) / warm if s < warm else 0.5 * (1 + math.cos(math.pi * (s - warm) / max(1, steps - warm))))

import os
WS=os.getcwd()
PY=f"cd {WS} && HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 HF_HOME=/data/transformers .venv/bin/python"
L=open('results/jobs_main.txt').read().splitlines()
keep=[l for l in L if '_lr0.0002' in l or 'grad_id' in l]
base={'code':3.6,'gsm8k':3.3,'emotion':2.8}
lrj=[]
for lr in [5e-5,1e-4,5e-4]:
    for r in [128,8,32,2]:
        for t in ['code','gsm8k','emotion']:
            mem=base[t]+(0.3 if r>=64 else 0)
            tag=f"0.5B_{t}_r{r}_s0_lr{lr:g}"
            lrj.append(f"{mem:.1f}\t{WS}/results/runs/{tag}.json\t{PY} src/train_eval.py --model 0.5B --task {t} --rank {r} --seed 0 --lr {lr}")
s0=[l for l in keep if '_s1_' not in l]; s1=[l for l in keep if '_s1_' in l]
# running/done lr jobs from the old block (5e-4/1e-3) are kept only if already started
started=[l for l in L if ('_lr0.0005' in l or '_lr0.001' in l) and (os.path.exists(l.split('\t')[1]) or os.path.exists(l.split('\t')[1]+'.lock'))]
started=[l for l in started if l not in lrj and l.split('\t')[1] not in [x.split('\t')[1] for x in lrj]]
open('results/jobs_main.txt','w').write('\n'.join(s0+lrj+s1+started)+'\n')
print(len(s0),len(lrj),len(s1),len(started))
EOF

Update 2026-10-26 (lora_rank_blind_spots workspace, ~170 LoRA train+eval jobs of Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B, HF+peft, no vLLM):
- GPUs had 0.5–6 GB free at 10:40, then ~25–43 GB freed on 3 GPUs at ~11:24 for ~10 min. A queue that only launches one job per GPU every 75 s wastes such a window; LAUNCH_GAP≈20–30 s filled it.
- Without a concurrency cap my queue launched 52 jobs → load avg 60 on 32 cores, each job 5× slower. Cap running jobs (~15–20) and set OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 per job.
- Mid-run OOMs from co-tenants: reserving memory at start (`torch.empty(RESERVE_GB)`, then del → it stays in PyTorch's cache) and saving the LoRA adapter right after training (so eval-only retries are possible) stopped most of the lost work. Real peak for a 0.5B LoRA job was 2.3–4.8 GB, more than estimated. HF generate prefill on 32 prompts × ~50 tokens still allocates ~0.5 GB of full-vocab logits.
- After gradient_checkpointing_disable(), pass use_cache=True to generate explicitly.
- Timings under contention: 0.5B LoRA, 250 steps, bs16 → 1.5 min (short classification inputs, idle GPU) up to 25–30 min (GSM8K/code, ~20 co-running jobs).
EOF

main_df = df[np.isclose(df.lr, MAIN_LR)]
    # ---------- summary table ----------

            .reset_index())
    summ.to_csv(os.path.join(R, "summary_table.csv"), index=False)

    # ---------- knees ----------
    knees = []
    for model in MODELS:
        for task in TASKS:
            s = summ[(summ.model == model) & (summ.task == task) & (summ["rank"] > 0)].set_index("rank")
            if not set(RANKS) <= set(s.index):
                continue
            means, ses = [], []
            for r in RANKS:
                M, _ = item_matrix(main_df, model, task, r)
                pm = M.mean(0)  # per-item mean over seeds
                means.append(pm.mean())
                # SE combining item sampling and seed variance (bootstrap over items of the seed-mean)
                ses.append(pm.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(pm)))
            means = np.array(means)
            k05, best, delta = knee_from_curve(means, ses, RANKS, 0.005)
            k1, _, _ = knee_from_curve(means, [0] * len(RANKS), RANKS, 0.01)
            nll = s.loc[RANKS, "nll"].values
            z = summ[(summ.model == model) & (summ.task == task) & (summ["rank"] == 0)]
            nll0 = z.nll.values[0] if len(z) else np.nan
            gain = nll0 - nll
            k_nll95 = RANKS[int(np.argmax(gain >= 0.95 * gain.max()))]
            k_nll99 = RANKS[int(np.argmax(gain >= 0.99 * gain.max()))]
            knees.append(dict(model=model, task=task, best_rank=best, knee=k05, knee_delta=delta, knee_1pp=k1,
                              knee_nll95=k_nll95, knee_nll99=k_nll99, best_nll_rank=RANKS[int(np.argmin(nll))],
                              best_metric=means.max(), r8_metric=means[RANKS.index(8)],
                              zero_shot=z.metric.values[0] if len(z) else np.nan,
                              n_seeds=int(s.n_seeds.min())))
    knees = pd.DataFrame(knees)
    knees.to_csv(os.path.join(R, "knees.csv"), index=False)
    print(knees.to_string())

    # ---------- rank-8 gaps (paired bootstrap over items) ----------
